messages:
kevin: Heads-up — I'm proposing we migrate away from the routing_hash index and start using route_key as the canonical routing column in telemetry/console datasets. Want quick feedback on risks and rollout plan.

sasha: +1 on concept. what's the main driver? is this about cardinality, human-readable keys, or cross-tenant routing?

kevin: All of the above. routing_hash was a legacy compacted value (opaque int) that causes pain for console queries and cross-join debugging. route_key is deterministic, stable across rollouts, and lets us join on route metadata without extra lookups. Also simplifies quota joins.

maya: Curious about index size and perf. routing_hash index is tiny and heavily used. route_key will be larger (string). Any benchmark?

kevin: We ran a small perf run on dev with a 3B row sample: single-column btree on route_key increased index size ~3.1x, query latency for hot lookups ~1.2x without caching. But KV prefix caching reduces tail significantly.

devon: Can we avoid downtime? need to keep the old index around until console + billing queries are migrated. dual-write? shadow-read?

kevin: Plan: dual-write to both columns at API layer for 2 weeks, enable shadow reads on a % of console traffic (10% -> 50% -> 100%), then schedule index drop. Backfill script optionally for historical rows.

aria: Backfill concerns: full-table updates will hammer PG. We should chunk by partition + time window and pause between batches. Also surface progress to the console team.

kevin: Agreed. Draft backfill SQL (example):
```sql
-- chunked update by created_at window
WITH batch AS (
  SELECT id FROM telemetry.events
  WHERE route_key IS NULL AND created_at >= '2025-03-01'::timestamptz
  ORDER BY created_at
  LIMIT 10000
)
UPDATE telemetry.events e
SET route_key = (SELECT compute_route_key_from_meta(e.meta))
FROM batch b
WHERE e.id = b.id;
```
We'll run via our backfill runner and throttle to 50 qps.

sasha: compute_route_key_from_meta needs to be deterministic and versioned. If logic changes later we need a version column or replay ability.

kevin: Will add route_key_version (int) and migration_id to write path so backfills can set the correct version.

devon: Dashboard UX: console queries that group by route should fall back to routing_hash when route_key is null. We'll need a migration-layer shim in query builder. That adds complexity.

maya: Also update quotas service — many quota joins currently use routing_hash. If we dual-write, quotas will need to accept both keys (prefer route_key if present). That could be a subtle bug source.

aria: Operational checklist suggestion:
• Create feature flag to enable dual-write (api-layer) per cluster
• Deploy backfill job with partitioned windows and rate limits
• Shadow reads in console (10/50/100 rollout)
• Update quota service to read route_key with fallback
• Add dashboard for backfill progress + error rates
• SRE oncall runbook for index pressure and vacuuming

kevin: Love it. ETA estimates: dual-write: 2 days, backfill infra + runner config: 3 days, gradual shadow reads: 1 week monitoring + fixes, full index drop: after 2 weeks at 100% shadow reads and no errors.

sasha: What about historical analytics stored in OLAP (warehouse)? We should pipeline a small copy that preserves both keys so long-running reports stay correct during transition.

kevin: Good call. We'll add a transformer step in the batch pipeline to emit route_key alongside routing_hash for 4 weeks post-switch.

ingest-bot: backfill-runner scheduled: staging job queued (job-id: bf-20250315-001) — will report progress to #eng-platform-backfills.

maya: Any rollback plan if we see latency regressions?

devon: Rollback: toggle feature flag to stop dual-write, switch console and quotas back to routing_hash only (instant), pause backfills. That should be safe because we never delete routing_hash until after safety window.

kevin: Need approvals from console, quotas, and SRE. @sasha @aria can you own console + quota compatibility checks? I'll coordinate the backfill and add migration docs.

sasha: I can take console compatibility and the query-shim. I'll wire a canary dashboard for top-10 heavy queries.

aria: I'll own SRE/runbook and quota service changes. I'll add alerts for index bloat and long-running vacuums.

kevin: Great — I'll draft the migration PR and runbook tonight and ping for review tomorrow. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

maya: Quick note: update the SDK docs and query examples so new users start with route_key. Otherwise we'll keep reintroducing routing_hash.

kevin: Will do. Last_message: I'll post the PR link when ready and schedule a 30-min sync if needed.
